sentences.text: Dolosigranulum pigrum is a commensal bacterium of the human nasopharynx that has been put forward as potentially protective.
Among 140 children sampled by nasopharyngeal aspirate, it was detected in 79 of them, including 44 of 65 healthy children.
That study reported it more often in healthy children than in invasive pneumococcal disease cases, and more often in boys than girls.
In a longitudinal nasopharyngeal cohort, it and Corynebacterium species were less abundant in patients who went on to develop post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2.
In the same cohort, antibiotic use was associated with lower levels of these commensal taxa.
